rv.q: What they don't do is throw themselves all the way into the material's glorious heights or its startlingly painful depths.
The result is a serviceable production that lacks fresh revelations.
The result is a brisk rendition of the story performed in a little under four quick hours (including two intermissions) that showcases the versatility of a 16-actor ensemble.
The cast, which frequently doubles and even triples up on roles, is superb.

cn.t: Critics find this solid revival of Shakespeare's compressed "Henry IV" more workmanlike than revelatory, praising its ambition to combine both plays while noting the production doesn't fully capture the material's comic brilliance or emotional devastation.
